person.name: Zaha_Hadid
person.summary: Zaha Hadid was an Iraqi British architect whose paintings and buildings used fractured, flowing geometry to reshape museums, cultural venues, and civic projects. After years of unbuilt competition designs, she completed major works across Europe, Asia, and the United States and became the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

conclusion: Zaha Hadid is recognized as a key figure in late-20th- and early-21st-century architecture. Her major completed works include the MAXXI Museum in Rome, Guangzhou Opera House, the London Aquatics Centre, Phaeno Science Center, and the Broad Art Museum.

events.title: Birth in Baghdad
events.description: Zaha Hadid is born into an upper-class family in Baghdad. Her father, Muhammad al-Hajj Husayn Hadid, is an industrialist and political figure. Her mother, Wajiha al-Sabunji, is an artist from Mosul. Her brother Foulath is part of the household.

events.title: Studies Mathematics in Beirut
events.description: Zaha Hadid studies mathematics at the American University of Beirut in Lebanon. She had attended boarding schools in England and Switzerland during the 1960s.

events.title: Moves to London
events.description: Zaha Hadid leaves Beirut for London to study at the Architectural Association School of Architecture. Rem Koolhaas, Elia Zenghelis, and Bernard Tschumi teach her there. She develops projects through large abstract paintings influenced by the [[Russian avant-garde|Russian avant-garde]], an early twentieth-century movement in abstract art and design.

images.caption: Architectural Association School of Architecture, London
images.creator: Kaihsu Tai

Russian avant-garde.explanation: Artists and designers in this movement experimented with abstraction, geometric form, and new visual languages before and after the Russian Revolution.

events.background:
The Architectural Association had become a center for radical architectural ideas before Hadid arrived. Elia Zenghelis had taught there since 1963. He became known for bringing avant-garde work into the curriculum. He later recalled that the school had built connections with architects and experimental groups across borders.

Her teachers remembered an unusually forceful approach to design. Rem Koolhaas called her “a planet in her own orbit” at graduation. Zenghelis said students called her the inventor of “the 89 degrees.” He recalled that she cared most about the overall composition. He said she left construction details such as staircases and joinery for others to resolve later.

events.title: Joins Office for Metropolitan Architecture
events.description: Zaha Hadid graduates from the Architectural Association School of Architecture in London. Her thesis, Malevich's Tektonik, proposes a 14-level hotel over Hungerford Bridge. She joins the Office for Metropolitan Architecture, an architecture firm in Rotterdam, where she works with Rem Koolhaas and Elia Zenghelis. Architectural engineer Peter Rice supports her early career.

events.title: Opens London Practice
events.description: Zaha Hadid opens Zaha Hadid Architects in London. She begins teaching at the Architectural Association School of Architecture. She produces highly detailed drawings for radical architectural proposals. Most of the proposals remain unbuilt.

events.title: Wins The Peak Competition
events.description: Zaha Hadid wins the competition for The Peak Leisure Club, a proposed recreation complex above Hong Kong. Her design sets sharp horizontal forms across the hillside. The drawings are widely published, though the project remains unbuilt. Patrik Schumacher begins an early association with her practice after encountering the design.

images.caption: Model of The Peak resort, Hong Kong
images.creator: Gary Berkovich

events.title: Exhibits at MoMA
events.description: The Museum of Modern Art in New York includes Zaha Hadid among seven architects in Deconstructivism in Architecture. Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley curate the exhibition, which presents buildings and drawings with fragmented forms and disrupted geometry. The exhibition brings Hadid's work before an international audience.

deconstructivism.explanation: Deconstructivism became a label for late twentieth-century architecture that broke with stable, rectilinear composition and emphasized collision, fragmentation, and instability.

events.title: Completes Vitra Fire Station
events.description: Rolf Fehlbaum invites Zaha Hadid to design a fire station for Vitra, a furniture company with a campus in Weil am Rhein. The Vitra Fire Station is completed in raw concrete and glass. Sharp diagonal forms meet at the building's center.

images.caption: Vitra Fire Station at Vitra Campus
images.creator: Marsupium

events.title: Opens Contemporary Arts Center
events.description: The Contemporary Arts Center opens in Cincinnati, Ohio, in a building designed by Zaha Hadid. Hadid wins the competition against Rem Koolhaas and other architects. She becomes the first woman to design an art museum in the United States. A 30-meter black stairway connects the galleries between curving and angular concrete walls.

images.caption: Contemporary Arts Center, Cincinnati
images.creator: No machine-readable author provided. Lanskeith17 assumed (based on copyright claims).

events.title: Receives Pritzker Prize
events.description: Zaha Hadid receives the [[Pritzker Architecture Prize|Pritzker Architecture Prize]] at the State Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg. She is the first woman to receive the award. Thomas Pritzker notes that she has completed four buildings.

Pritzker Architecture Prize.explanation: The Pritzker Architecture Prize is an annual international award for architects whose work shows significant talent and achievement. Hadid was the first woman to receive it.

events.background:
The four completed projects cited with the award ranged from the Vitra Fire Station to the Bergisel ski jump in Innsbruck. They also included the Hoenheim North car park and terminus in France and the Contemporary Arts Center in Cincinnati.

Thomas Pritzker said that this small body of work had already won Hadid great acclaim. He also pointed to the promise he saw in her energy and ideas.

events.title: Opens Phaeno Science Center
events.description: Phaeno Science Center opens in Wolfsburg, Germany. Zaha Hadid designs the museum seven meters above the ground. Ten inverted cone-shaped concrete supports hold up the exhibition spaces. The supports contain entrances, shops, and a cafe beneath the building.

events.title: Opens MAXXI Museum
events.description: Rome's [[MAXXI Museum|MAXXI Museum]] opens in a building designed by Zaha Hadid for contemporary art and architecture. Its galleries follow curving routes beneath linear skylights that filter daylight. Patrik Schumacher participates in planning the project. Hadid receives the Stirling Prize for the building later that year.

MAXXI Museum.explanation: MAXXI is Italy's national museum of twenty-first-century arts in Rome. Its name comes from Museo nazionale delle arti del XXI secolo.

events.background:
Work on the museum extended from 1998 to 2010. Hadid used the orthogonal grids of the surrounding site to set out its overall form. Smooth white walls and a black-and-white palette connect the exterior to an earlier phase of her work.

Groups of five thin pylons raise the building above the ground. One glass-fronted gallery projects over the plaza and casts shade below. Inside, black steel stairs and bridges cross a central void. White light glows beneath them. Rowan Moore described the galleries as bending oblong tubes that overlap, intersect, and pile over one another. Hadid said she wanted the building to produce “confluence, interference and turbulence.”

events.title: Guangzhou Opera House
events.description: Zaha Hadid designs Guangzhou Opera House in Guangzhou, China, after winning an international competition in 2002. The complex takes the form of two smooth-edged volumes. It contains an 1,800-seat theater, a multipurpose theater, an entry hall, and a salon.

events.title: Olympic Venue and Damehood
events.description: Hadid's London Aquatics Centre hosts swimming events for the 2012 Summer Olympics. Its sweeping roof spans the competition pools and spectator seating. Elizabeth II makes Hadid a Dame for services to architecture.

images.caption: London Aquatics Centre
images.creator: Tom Parnell from Scottish Borders, Scotland

events.title: Opens Broad Art Museum
events.description: The Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum opens at Michigan State University in East Lansing, Michigan. Zaha Hadid designs its sloping, pleated stainless-steel facades. The galleries hold modern and contemporary art.

images.caption: MSU Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum
images.creator: Dj1997

events.title: Receives Royal Gold Medal
events.description: The Royal Institute of British Architects awards Zaha Hadid its Royal Gold Medal in London. She is the first woman to receive the medal as an individual recipient.

events.title: Death in Miami
events.description: Zaha Hadid is in Miami for treatment of [[bronchitis|bronchitis]]. She suffers a heart attack and dies at Mount Sinai Medical Center on March 31, 2016.

bronchitis.explanation: Bronchitis is inflammation of the airways that carry air to the lungs. Hadid was in Miami receiving treatment for this illness when she suffered the heart attack that caused her death.
